faq.q: What link formats does the timestamp generator produce?
faq.a: From a video URL and an H:M:S time (or a typed time like 1:23:45) it builds four links: a watch URL with t=<seconds>s, a watch URL with t=1h2m3s, a youtu.be short link with ?t=<seconds>, and an embed URL with ?start=<seconds>. This matters because the parameter name differs — embeds use start=, not t=, so using t= on an embed does nothing.

faq.q: How does the Chapter Builder check YouTube's rules?
faq.a: It validates the five conditions YouTube requires for chapters to appear: the first timestamp must be 00:00, there must be at least 3 chapters, each must be at least 10 seconds long, timestamps must be in ascending order, and all times must be valid. Each rule shows a pass/fail tick, and if order is wrong it offers a one-click 'Sort them' button.

faq.q: My chapters drifted after I re-edited the video — can I fix them?
faq.a: Yes. Enter a positive or negative number of seconds in the Offset field and Apply Offset shifts every timestamp uniformly, which handles the common case where trimming the start pushes all later chapters out of sync. You can also paste an existing description or rough list and the Paste-Parse feature converts lines like '1:30 Topic' into editable rows.

faq.q: What does the Embed Code tab generate?
faq.a: A full iframe embed for any YouTube URL, with optional start and end times (entered as seconds or mm:ss), plus autoplay and mute checkboxes. It assembles the correct start=, end=, autoplay=1, and mute=1 parameters. Your chapter list and recent videos are saved in your browser (yt_ts_chapters, yt_hist) so a long chapter list survives a reload.
